newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends up on cautious mood.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends up on cautious mood.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended slightly up with investors taking a wait-and-see attitude after continued gains over the past few days, brokers said.
The index edged up 0.235 points or 0.34 percent to 68.726 points on volume of 23 million shares worth $9.7 million.

"Investors are cautious after the index failed to breach 69 points this afternoon," said one broker. "That level is regarded as a key resistance level and if it is breached, B shares are likely to rise further.
"The market ignored the tumble in A shares late in the session which shows market sentiment is steady with investors buying shares for the long term," a second broker said.
"The market will move up further if there is no negative news in the short term, as the technical charts look very good," he said.
Of 43 B shares, 42 traded, with 18 up, eight flat and 16 down.
Shanghai Vacuum and Electron Device was the star on bargain-hunting, jumping $0.014 or 7.29 percent to $0.206 on volume of 1.2 million shares.
The SSE30 index dipped 54.033 points or 1.88 percent to 2,820.326 points.
Tsingtao Brewery was the biggest loser on institutional unwinding, slumping 0.39 yuan or 5.27 percent to 7.01 yuan on volume of 3.7 million shares.
Clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai traded the most on institutional buying, gaining $0.01 or 2.71 percent to $0.378 on volume of 2.4 million shares.
Shanghai A shares fell sharply in the afternoon session on profit-taking after sharp gains over the past few weeks, brokers said, adding that the market needs some time to correct in the short term.
The index slipped 17.325 points or 1.55 percent to 1,099.467 points on volume of 733.4 million shares worth seven billion yuan.
